methodological_rigor.justification: The single-center retrospective study (160 patients; 86 PCa, 74 BPH) uses a pathological reference standard (biopsy or prostatectomy within 2 weeks of MRI) and dual blinded readers with a reported ICC of 0.992 for APTw measurements. Statistical methods (DeLong test, ROC analysis, Spearman correlation, multivariate logistic regression) are appropriate, but the same cohort is used to derive and evaluate the combined APTw+PI-RADS model without external validation or a bootstrapped/internal cross-validation scheme. The PSA 'gray zone' and high-risk subgroup analyses have modest sample sizes (acknowledged), cutoff selection is not prespecified, and no adjustment for multiple comparisons is described.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Diagnostic case-control design with retrospective single-center sampling corresponds to Oxford LoE 3b. The added value of APTw over PI-RADS v2.1 and its robustness in the PSA gray zone and transition zone are clinically useful if validated, offering a plausible noninvasive adjunct for PCa risk stratification but not yet practice-changing.

reporting_quality.justification: As a diagnostic accuracy study, STARD applies. Inclusion/exclusion criteria, index tests, reference standard, blinding, inter-reader agreement (ICC, Bland-Altman), and AUCs with sensitivity/specificity are well reported. However, there is no STARD flow diagram, indeterminate/excluded cases are not tabulated, cutoff derivation is not prespecified, calibration and 95% CIs for some subgroup AUCs are partial, and no data/code availability statement is provided beyond referencing R software.

novelty_literature.justification: APTw MRI in prostate cancer has been reported before (e.g., Jia 2011, Takayama 2016 cited), and the present study extends prior work by directly comparing/combining with PI-RADS v2.1 and testing performance in the PSA gray zone and transition zone. This is a meaningful incremental extension rather than a first-in-class application; the combined APTw+PI-RADS model and subgroup-focused evaluation provide novelty but within an established line of research.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written, well organized, and uses appropriate clinical terminology. Figures and tables are succinctly described with sensible interpretations, and the discussion appropriately acknowledges confounders (pH, MT, T1) that may affect APTw signal. Minor issues include missing spaces, occasional awkward phrasing, and reliance on only two summary tables with limited raw subgroup tabulation.

key_strengths: High inter-reader agreement (ICC 0.992) with Bland-Altman and dual-rater blinded APTw measurements
Combined APTw + PI-RADS v2.1 model significantly improves AUC over PI-RADS alone (0.915 vs 0.875, p<0.05)
Clinically relevant subgroup analyses in transition zone and PSA gray zone with APTw outperforming PSA (AUC 0.80 vs 0.75)
Positive correlation between APTw and Gleason Score (Spearman rho 0.407) supports biological plausibility
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design with no external validation; cutoffs derived on the same dataset
Modest high-risk (GS >=8) and PSA gray zone subgroup sizes limit power and CI precision
Reporting does not explicitly follow STARD and lacks a participant flow diagram
APTw signal confounders (pH, MT, T1) acknowledged but not modeled; no multipool CEST quantification
chief_reviewer.rationale: A well-conducted but single-center diagnostic study with solid reader agreement and clear incremental value of APTw over PI-RADS; suitable for a mid-tier oncology/radiology journal pending external validation and STARD-aligned reporting.
